Demolitions and Relocations
Because of the dilapidated condition of some houses, rehabilitation may not be economically feasible and demolition will occur. The City of San Jose Poverty and Code Enforcement Department estimates that twenty structures may require demolition. Additionally, another 160 dwelling units may require such substantial rehabilitation that the tenants will have to temporarily be relocated. The demolitions, requiring permanent occupant relocation, and the intensive rehabilitations requiring temporary relocation, are expected to be concentrated in the Mayfair and Gardner neighborhoods. Reuse of the sites of demolitions is limited to residential, primarily with "move-ons" of existing dwelling units. As a result of clearance of homes in the San Jose Municipal Airport vicinity, homes are available at auction by the City.
The City has established a policy of giving priority to families displaced by redevelopment and other activities in securing these houses. However, due to the stringent requirements involved in bringing a relocated structure up to code, it is probable that residents of the neighborhood vitalization areas will require one or more forms of financial assistance in order to purchase any of these units. Typically, they are bought by movers or contractors, relocated, brought up to code and then resold. By arranging for such housing prior to demolition, the negative impact of displacement on residents who wish to remain in the neighborhood could be greatly mitigated. The proposed Housing Assistance Plan will also serve to mitigate potential negative impacts resulting from relocation.
